placements.why: This envelope is an observatory calibration record — an instrument's tuned frequency verified against dated reference plates. Nothing in the (currently empty) strata covers organizational categories at all, and calibration/verification work is plausibly a recurring organizational category future envelopes (other instruments, other verification runs) will keep feeding, not a one-off fact — so it needs its own top-level strata home rather than folding under an unrelated category.
placements.title: Instrument calibration and verification as an organizational practice
placements.frame: What instruments, calibration checks, or verification runs does the organization perform, and what reference standards do they confirm against?

placements.title: Calibration verification confirms an instrument's readiness against established reference standards
placements.frame: Does this verification event show the instrument's calibration holding against its established reference standard across the operating range claimed?
placements.why: src-1 asserts the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration was checked against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band — a verification-against-standard claim, not a one-time measurement in isolation, since the underlying practice (tune, then verify against a dated reference set) is the kind of subject later calibration envelopes for this or other instruments would keep feeding. src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument identity and calibration/verification facts in field-label form and carry no separate theme, so they support the same leaf rather than minting their own. The specific value (88.4 MHz) and the specific reference set (June plates) are the evidentiary facts for this leaf, not leaves themselves, per the narrative-grain test.
